title: Own and cancel the HostSource sampler thread without panicking app construction
description:
## Finding

Every `HostSource` starts an OS thread but retains no join handle. Construction panics if the thread cannot be created, while drop merely sets a flag observed after an uninterruptible one-second sleep. The sampler can therefore outlive its tile/source generation and there is no proof it stopped before app replacement or process teardown.

## Evidence at audited commit

* `crates/gtui-query/src/host.rs:28-58` allocates shared state and calls `std::thread::Builder::spawn(...).expect(...)`.
* `HostSource` stores only the ring and stop flag, not the `JoinHandle`.
* The worker sleeps with `std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(1))`, so cancellation cannot wake it promptly.
* `Drop` at lines 92-97 sets the flag and returns without joining.
* Observe construction occurs synchronously from the compositor's lazy-load path, so thread-spawn exhaustion unwinds the UI unless caught above it.
* A source remains owned by a detached query engine until any current query returns; tile drop is not a generation fence for the sampler.

## Impact

Repeated enable/disable/reload or failed app generations can leave overlapping samplers temporarily active, produce stale work after teardown, and make exact lifecycle/resource tests impossible. Process/thread exhaustion turns opening the optional Observe tab into a host panic.

## Implementation constraints

* Make construction fallible and surface the error as a failed app slot.
* Own a cancellation token plus join handle; use an interruptible wait rather than fixed sleep.
* Define a strict shutdown bound and typed outcome. Never detach on the ordinary path.
* Bind sampler results to the source generation and prevent post-cancel publication.
* Coordinate query-engine task cancellation so source drop is not indefinitely delayed by a hung remote panel.
* Avoid one sampler per consumer where a safely shared host metrics supervisor already exists.

## Acceptance criteria

* Injected thread-spawn failure is visible and does not unwind the compositor.
* Drop/shutdown wakes and joins an idle sampler within a small deterministic bound.
* Repeated construction/destruction returns thread count to baseline.
* No sample is appended after cancellation acknowledgement.
* A hung query cannot retain HostSource past the app shutdown deadline.
* Tests cover lock poisoning, sampler failure/panic, clock failure, and concurrent final query/teardown.
